title: Adding edges cannot increase the number of connected components
statement: Let $H$ and $K$ be two simple graphs on a common finite vertex set $V$, and suppose $H \le K$, meaning that every edge of $H$ is also an edge of $K$. Then $K$ has no more connected components than $H$; that is, the number of connected components of $K$ is at most the number of connected components of $H$.
hypotheses_covered: H and K are simple graphs on the same vertex set
H ≤ K (every edge of H is an edge of K)
replaced:
\textbf{Component count is antitone in the subgraph order.}  If \texttt{H $\le$ K} then
\texttt{$\omega$(K) $\le$ $\omega$(H)} --- adding edges can only merge components.
